title: Homepage hero hypotheses and variants
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects fresh hero / fold hypotheses, supporting microcopy, quick competitive notes and a lightweight test plan for the homepage and product landing CTAs. Goal is to identify 2–3 distinct hero directions to A/B test in Q2 that signal Redwood Inference's production-first positioning without leaning on technical jargon only engineers get.

Audience segments we want to serve on the first fold:
- Engineer evaluating latency/cost for an LLM feature (primary).
- Platform/infra buyer evaluating predictable throughput for their org.
- Product PM/Founder validating time-to-value and ease of integration.

Topline positioning premise:
- Core claim: "Inference as a predictable platform" — not just model access. Distinguish with operational guarantees, routing/fallbacks, and cost controls. Keep phrasing concrete (latency, cost, reliability) and avoid vague words like "best".

Variant A — "Predictable inference, everywhere" (latency & SLAs)
- Hero headline candidates:
  - "Predictable LLM inference at production scale"
  - "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and SLOs"
- Subhead options:
  - "Hosted API, dedicated capacity, or private deployment—same API, consistent latency and reliability."
  - "Pin model versions, set latency SLOs, and fall back automatically when capacity is limited."
- Primary CTA: "Try hosted API — free tier"
- Supporting proof bullets (3 short):
  - "Multi-region routing with automated fallback"
  - "SLA-backed dedicated pools for steady throughput"
  - "Token-level latency breakdowns in Console"
- Hypothesis: engineers care most about predictability; this reduces time-to-trust and increases trial-to-paid conversion.

Variant B — "Cost-transparent serving" (unit economics & tooling)
- Hero headline candidates:
  - "Make LLM economics predictable and controllable"
  - "Lower unit costs with smart batching, cache and routing policies"
- Subhead options:
  - "Per-token cost visibility, quantization profiles, and automated batching suggestions."
  - "Optimize throughput without sacrificing output quality."
- Primary CTA: "Estimate costs for your workload"
- Supporting proof bullets:
  - "Automated batching and prefix cache save up to 60% per-token"
  - "Guided quantization profiles for common model classes"
  - "Cost attribution per route and token in the Console"
- Hypothesis: CTOs/platform teams will engage with a cost-focused flow and request demos/commits for Dedicated.

Variant C — "Unified runtime for any deployment" (developer experience & portability)
- Hero headline candidates:
  - "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"
  - "Develop once, run anywhere: hosted, reserved, or on-prem inference"
- Subhead options:
  - "Pin models, run canaries, and rollout with zero-code policy flips."
  - "Protect data with private control planes and KMS integrations."
- Primary CTA: "See how deployments compare"
- Supporting proof bullets:
  - "Private VPC control plane and on-prem option"
  - "Rollouts: canary, A/B, auto-fallback"
  - "KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs for compliance"
- Hypothesis: enterprise buyers will convert faster if portability is explicit and low-friction.

Microcopy and fold-level blueprint (first 2 folds)
- First fold: single-line headline, 8–12 word subhead, 1–2 CTAs (primary and a secondary link to docs). Add a short social proof string below (customer logos or metrics).
- Second fold: 3-column feature snapshot mapping to Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Each column: 2-line description, 2 proof bullets, small CTA to compare pricing or request demo.

Product page copy hooks (short blurbs to use across product pages)
- Hosted API: "Quick to start, transparent to scale — get production-grade latency without ops overhead."
- Dedicated: "Reserved GPU capacity with predictable throughput and SLA controls for business-critical workloads."
- Private: "Customer-managed control planes, optional on-prem packages, and enterprise key management for regulated data."
- Optimize toolkit: "Automated batching, cache, and quantization guidance that improve unit economics while preserving quality."

Competitive notes (concise)
- Comp A (managed endpoint clouds): strength = model catalog and scale; weakness = limited batching/caching controls and weaker cost transparency.
- Comp B (simple LLM APIs): strength = easy onboarding; weakness = no dedicated pools or private deployments with KMS integration.
- Comp C (self-host inference runtimes): strength = control & cost potential; weakness = high ops burden, missing unified console and rollout primitives.
- Net positioning: emphasize "production economics + low ops friction + deployment parity" as the space Redwood occupies between the three.

Quick QA on claims / guardrails
- Avoid explicit numeric claims like "X% cheaper" unless backed by a reproducible benchmark. Use phrasing like "reduce per-token cost for common workloads" or provide ranges only when supported by internal tests.
- When using latency numbers, tie to sample configs: e.g., "p99 latency under Xms on 8k context with dedicated pools" and reference an internal benchmark doc.

Test plan (lightweight)
- Test matrix: canonical traffic slice = embed prompt generator for search; chat completion for product feature; long-context summarization.
- Metrics: signups -> hosted API trial -> API calls/day -> upgrade to paid / request demo. Secondary: bounce rate, time-to-first-API-call, docs clicks.
- Experiment cadence: run 3 hero variants simultaneously for 4 weeks with equal traffic allocation, measure trial-to-paid at 4 and 8 weeks and click-through rate to pricing.

Implementation notes for design/dev
- Keep hero responsive: headline should collapse to a single line on small screens; test truncated subhead for mobile.
- CTA flow: primary CTA goes to self-serve signup + prefilled sample request that triggers a quick guided tour in Console. Secondary CTA to "Compare deployments" anchors to second fold.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Which hero metric will be the single north-star for the experiment? Recommend trial-to-paid within 8 weeks.
- Do we want to surface a benchmark number in one hero variant? If yes, we need a reproducible benchmark and sign-off from Applied ML and SRE.
- Should social proof be logos or short objective metrics (e.g., "used in production by 35 engineering teams")? Design preference recommended: logos + short metric if available.

Next steps
- Align on top-2 hero variants by 2026-03-20.
- Engineering to scaffold experiment routes and prefill flows by 2026-03-27.
- Applied ML / SRE to provide benchmark artifacts if we surface numbers by 2026-03-24.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally written with rough phrasings and multiple short options per claim. Please mark preferred headline (A/B/C) in comments and flag any compliance-sensitive phrasing.

Rough change log:
- 2026-02-15 initial draft by Priya
- 2026-02-19 added cost-focused variant (Ethan)
- 2026-02-28 added portability variant (Marisol)
- 2026-03-10 consolidated into testable matrix and updated timelines

End.
